HB 634, sponsored by Rep. Brett Easterbrook, R-Fruitdale, levies a 4% lodging tax in Washington County. The bill passed 17-0. It moves to the Senate.
HB 635, sponsored by Rep. Brett Easterbrook, R-Fruitdale, authorizes the Choctaw County Commission to hold a referendum on a property tax increase of up to 5 mills to be used exclusively for county road and bridge improvement. The bill passed 12-0. It goes to the Senate.
HB 639, sponsored by Rep. Alan Baker, R-Brewton, authorizes municipalities in Escambia County to operate an automated photographic speeding enforcement system. The bill passed 14-0. It moves to the Senate.
HB 591, sponsored by Rep. Rex Reynolds, R-Huntsville, makes supplemental appropriations from the Rural Health Transformation Program to the Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs for the fiscal year ending Sept. 30, 2026 and creates the Joint Legislative Oversight Committee on Rural Health Transformation Program Funds. The bill passed 104-0. It moves to the Senate.
HB 614, sponsored by Rep. Rex Reynolds, R-Huntsville, makes supplemental appropriations from the Rural Health Transformation Program to the Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs for the fiscal year ending Sept. 30, 2027. The bill passed 101-0. It moves to the Senate.
SB 143, sponsored by Sen. Greg Albritton, R-Atmore, removes a sunset clause on supplemental privilege assessment, secondary supplemental assessments and surcharges for beds in nursing facilities. The bill passed 102-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
SB 144, Sen. Greg Albritton, R-Atmore, removes a sunset clause for a quarterly assessment payment for emergency medical transport providers, and makes the quarterly payment for Medicaid maintenance permanent. The bill passed 104-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.\
SB 145, sponsored by Sen. Greg Albritton, R-Atmore, removes a sunset clause for private hospitals that pay a provider privilege tax to the Alabama Medicaid Agency and makes the tax permanent. The bill passed 104-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
SB 152, sponsored by Sen. Greg Albritton, R-Atmore, allows for other revenue sources to fund the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP). The bill passed 104-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 224, sponsored by Rep. A.J. McCampbell, allows for other revenue sources to fund the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP). The bill passed 103-0. It moves to the Senate.
SB 153, sponsored by Sen. Greg Albritton, R-Atmore, appropriated $36.6 million to the Children First Trust Fund for fiscal year 2027. The bill passed 103-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
SB 154, sponsored by Sen. Greg Albritton, R-Atmore, provided a 2% cost of living raise to all state employees, which will be distributed to employees on the first pay day on or after Oct. 1, if passed into law. The bill passed 97-0. It goes back to the Senate for concurrence or a conference committee.
SB 162, sponsored by Sen. Greg Albritton, R-Atmore, appropriates $169,000 to the Coalition Against Domestic Violence for fiscal year 2027 and requires an annual audit from the coalition for funding to be released. The bill passed 102-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
Members of the House of Representatives gathered in the Old Chambers in the Alabama State Capitol in Montgomery, Alabama, on April 1, 2026. The session was the first legislative session held in the Old House Chambers since 2009. (Anna Barrett/Alabama Reflector)
SB 317, sponsored by Sen. Arthur Orr, R-Decatur, creates the Alabama Commission on the Evaluation of Services to evaluate programs and their costs proposed by the Legislature within 30 days of each regular and special session. The bill passed 102-0. It goes back to the Senate for concurrence or a conference committee.
SB 226, sponsored by Sen. Greg Albritton, R-Atmore, appropriates $836 million in supplemental funds for the rest of fiscal year 2026 for state agencies. The bill passed 102-0. It goes back to the Senate for concurrence or a conference committee.
SB 146, sponsored by Sen. Greg Albritton, R-Atmore, appropriates $3.7 billion for state agencies in the state General Fund budget for fiscal year 2027. The bill passed 104-0. It goes back to the Senate for concurrence or a conference committee.
HB 266, sponsored by Rep. Chris Sells, R-Greenville, raised the penalty for reckless endangerment to a Class C felony punishable up to one year in prison if an individual recklessly engages in conduct that could seriously injure multiple people and a Class B felony punishable up to 20 years in prison if a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument is used while performing the reckless action. The House concurred with Senate changes 99-1. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 282, sponsored by Rep. Jim Hill, R-Odenville, changes the start date of the terms of members of the Alabama Board of Pardons and Paroles from July 1 to March 1. The House concurred with Senate changes 99-0. It goes to Ivey.
Senate
Sen. Sam Givhan, R-Huntsville, reading through the bills that are eligible for a vote by the Alabama Senate on April 1, 2026, on the floor of the Alabama Senate in Montgomery, Alabama. (Anna Barrett/Alabama Reflector)
SB 118, sponsored by Sen. Lance Bell, R-Pell City, creates the Alabama Background Check Service, which allows law enforcement to collect biometric identifiers for noncriminal justice purposes to identify individuals. The Senate concurred 32-0 with House changes. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
SB 374, sponsored by Sen. Billy Beasley, D-Clayton, sets an election for Henry County to consider a three-mill tax running from 2027 to 2034 to fund school projects in Headland. The measure, a constitutional amendment, passed 28-0. It goes to the House.
HB 432, sponsored by Rep Kenyatte Hassell, D-Montgomery, allows the Montgomery County Probate Judge to assess an “additional reasonable fee” for performing marriages. The bill passed 29-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
SB 375, sponsored by Sen. Linda Coleman-Madison, D-Birmingham, increases the Birmingham mayor’s expense allowance to $10,000 per month and puts the mayor’s compensation in control of the city council. The bill passed 30-0. It goes to the House.
SB 357, sponsored by Sen. Billy Beasley, D-Clayton, creates an 8% local tax on the net gambling revenue collected from the horse racing licensee of the Macon County Racing Commission. The bill passed 30-0. It goes to the House.
Sen. Linda Coleman-Madison, D-Birmingham, speaking to a colleague on the floor of the Alabama Senate on April 1, 2026, in Montgomery, Alabama. (Anna Barrett/Alabama Reflector)
HB 475, sponsored by Rep. Mack Butler, R-Rainbow City, expands the Public Service Commission from three to seven members, with those members being appointed by the governor this summer until they will be elected in staggered terms every two years starting in 2032. The bill passed 32-0 with a substitute and an amendment. The House later concurred 72-26. Gov. Kay Ivey signed the bill into law on Thursday.
HB 312, sponsored by Rep. Jim Hill, R-Odenville, makes new calculations determining district attorneys’ retirement plans in the Judicial Retirement Fund. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 225, sponsored by Rep. Ivan Smith, R-Clanton, requires boards of education to post notices of vacancies within seven calendar days instead of 14 days. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 266, sponsored by Rep. Chris Sells, R-Greenville, raises the penalty for reckless endangerment to a Class C felony punishable up to one year in prison if an individual recklessly engages in conduct that could seriously injure multiple people and a Class B felony punishable up to 20 years in prison if a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument is used while performing the reckless action. The bill passed 32-0 with an amendment. It goes to the House for concurrence or conference committee.
HB 267, sponsored by Rep. Chris Sells, R-Greenville, authorizes the State Forester to receive sickness and annual leave and reimbursement for travel. The bill passed 34-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 268, sponsored by Rep. Reed Ingram, R-Pike Road, authorizes the state 911 Board to monitor call statistics of local communication districts and share crime reporting data with the Alabama Attorney General’s Office. The bill passed 34-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
Sen. Matt Woods, R-Jasper, sitting on the floor of the Alabama Senate on April 1, 2026, in Montgomery, Alabama. (Anna Barrett/Alabama Reflector)
HB 132, sponsored by Rep. Tracy Estes, R-Winfield, updates the crime of second degree assault to include intent to harm a child in an educational environment if the person committing the crime is over 19 years old, not employed or enrolled in the educational space and causes physical injury to any person. The bill passed 34-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 282, sponsored by Rep. Jim Hill, R-Odenville, changes the start date of the terms of members of the Alabama Board of Pardons and Paroles from July 1 to March 1. The bill passed 34-0 with an amendment. It goes to the House for concurrence or conference committee.
HB 152, sponsored by Rep. Danny Garrett, R-Trussville, repeals the law requiring the University of Alabama to have a stand alone School of Social Work. The bill passed 34-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 128, sponsored by Rep. Marilyn Lands, D-Huntsville, authorizes the State Board of Midwifery to accept gifts and grants and makes technical revisions and updates to the law. The bill passed 34-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 86, sponsored by Rep. Chris England, D-Tuscaloosa, updates parole consideration to include an inmate’s employment status and education gained while incarcerated and allows the Board of Pardons and Paroles to consider the inmate’s low-risk to reoffend. The bill passed 34-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
SB 364, sponsored by Sen. Rodger Smitherman, D-Birmingham, would require public schools to provide classes on violence prevention, conflict resolution and mediation before high school graduation. The bill passed 34-0. It goes to the House.
SB 318, sponsored by Sen. Merika Coleman, D-Pleasant Grove, expands the crime of sexual torture. The bill passed 34-0. It goes to the House.

HB 646, sponsored by Rep. Sam Jones, D-Mobile, alters the boundary lines and corporate limits of the City of Semmes in Mobile County. The bill passed 26-0. It moves to the Senate.
HB 604, sponsored by Rep. Terri Collins, R-Decatur, establishes a standing accountability council to ensure accountability measures are supporting improved outcomes for students. The bill passed 93-1. It moves to the Senate.
SB 174, sponsored by Sen. Greg Albritton, R-Atmore, allows oil and gas wells to be converted to alternative energy facilities. The bill passed 85-3. It goes back to the Senate for concurrence or a conference committee.
SB 279, sponsored by Sen. Clyde Chambliss, R-Prattville, exempts certain services from getting a general contracting license, like pressure washing, floor waxing and security system maintenance. The bill passed 100-0. It goes to Ivey.
HB 579, sponsored by Rep. Ginny Shaver, R-Leesburg, exempts Tigers for Tomorrow Exotic Animal Preserve from sales and use taxes and authorizes local governments to provide similar exemptions. The bill passed 101-0. It goes to the Senate.
SB 219, sponsored by Sen. Wes Kitchens, R-Arab, requires all service contract provider registration fees to be paid to the State Treasury to fund the Special Examination Revolving Fund. The bill passed 99-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
SB 233, sponsored by Sen. Lance Bell, R-Pell City, changes the conditions for classifications of felonies for eluding an officer and elevates the base punishment from a Class A misdemeanor to a Class D felony, punishable by up to five years in person. The bill passed 80-15. It goes to Gov. Kay  Ivey.

SB 32, sponsored by Sen. Wes Kitchens, R-Arab, exempts households whose sole income is veterans’ benefits from paying solid waste collection fees. The bill passed 102-0. It goes back to the Senate for concurrence or a conference committee.
SB 197, sponsored by Sen. Dan Roberts, R-Mountain Brook, exempts mobile food vendors from local health and fire inspections as long as they get regular inspections from state authorities. The bill passed 103-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
SB 288, sponsored by, Sen. Tim Melson, R-Florence, requires agriculture boards to appoint their own successors, instead of the Legislature, every five years. The bill passed 99-1. It goes back to the Senate for concurrence or a conference committee.

HB 496, sponsored by Rep. Barbara Drummond, D-Mobile, allows adjoining homeowners to receive notice of municipal lien foreclosures and have bidding preference in foreclosures of municipal liens. The bill passed 30-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 500, sponsored by Rep. Napoleon Bracy, D-Prichard, requires three constables per House of Representative with territory in Mobile County. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 498, sponsored by Rep. Napoleon Bracy, D-Prichard, allows for the abatement and removal of weeds, overgrown grasses and inoperable motor vehicles on private property; allows for abandoned debris to be declared a public nuisance in the City of Prichard. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 501, sponsored by Rep. Napoleon Bracy, D-Prichard, establishes a procedure for the establishment, operation, modification, renewal and dissolution of self-help businesses in the City of Prichard. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
SB 376, sponsored by Sen. Jack Williams, R-Wilmer, alters the boundary lines and corporate limits of the City of Semmes in Mobile County. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to the House.
HB 502, sponsored by Rep. Napoleon Bracy, D-Prichard, allows the City of Prichard to file an expedited quiet title and foreclosure action in circuit court for abandoned tax sale properties within city limits. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 510, sponsored by Speaker Pro Tempore Chris Pringle, R-Mobile, gives industrial development boards in municipalities with a population between 175,000 and 299,999 residents to issue and sell bonds and to acquire, construct, expand, improve, replace, equip, maintain, operate, lease and dispose of development properties. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
Sen. Merika Coleman, D-Pleasant Grove, stands on the floor of the Alabama Senate on April 2, 2026 at the Alabama Statehouse in Montgomery, Alabama. (Brian Lyman/Alabama Reflector)
HB 629, sponsored by Rep. Shane Stringer, R-Citronelle, alters the boundary lines and corporate limits of the Town of Mt. Vernon in Mobile County. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 574, sponsored by Rep. Pebblin Warren, D-Tuskegee, changes the qualifying age from 70 to 75 for probate judge in Macon County. The measure, a constitutional amendment, passed 32-0. It goes on a future ballot to be considered by voters.
HB 613, sponsored by Rep. A.J. McCampbell, D-Linden, alters the boundary lines and corporate limits of the City of Demopolis in Marengo County. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 587, sponsored by Rep. Randy Wood, R-Anniston, establishes a service of process fee of $50 for the service or attempted service for matters pending or to be started in a court outside of Alabama, and a $100 service or attempted service fee for processing by the sheriff to an inmate at the federal correctional facility in Talladega County. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 573, sponsored by Rep. Thomas Jackson, D-Thomasville, allows a qualified tax payer who is 65 years old or older in Perry County to claim a senior property tax exemption. The measure, a constitutional amendment, passed 32-0. It goes on a future ballot to be considered by voters.
HB 624, sponsored by Rep. Kelvin Lawrence, D-Haleyville, increases the probate recording fee in Wilcox County from $5 to $10 for records filed in the office. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 625, sponsored by Rep. Chad Robertson, R-Heflin, allows the Cleburne County Revenue Commissioner to establish guidelines for electronic filing for the reporting, assessment and payment of business personal property taxes. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 636, sponsored by Rep. Brett Easterbrook, R-Fruitdale, repeals part of a 1984 law that sets the compensation for the Washington County circuit clerk. The bill passed 32-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
SB 379, sponsored by Sen. Wes Kitchens, R-Arab, alters the boundary lines and corporate limits of the City of Owens Cross Roads in Madison County The bill passed 32-0. It goes to the House.
HB 235, sponsored by Rep. Danny Garrett, R-Trussville, makes supplemental appropriations for the fiscal year ending in September from the Education Trust Fund to different agencies totaling $419 million and from gross income tax receipts from the CHOOSE Act Fund to the Alabama Department of Revenue for $100 million. The bill passed 33-0 with a substitute. It goes to the House for concurrence or conference committee.
HB 236, sponsored by Rep. Danny Garrett, R-Trussville, makes supplemental appropriations from the Education Trust Fund Advancement and Technology Fund for $1 billion for the fiscal year ending in September. The bill passed 33-0 with a substitute. It goes to the House for concurrence or conference committee.
HB 237, sponsored by Rep. Danny Garrett, R-Trussville, transfers $399 million from the Educational Opportunities Reserve Fund for the fiscal year ending in September to the Renewing Alabama’s Investment in Student Excellence (RAISE) Fund and makes appropriations from the Educational Opportunities Reserve Fund to various higher education institutions totaling $101 million. The bill passed 33-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 238, sponsored by Rep. Danny Garrett, R-Trussville, makes appropriations for the support, maintenance and development of public education in Alabama for fiscal year 2027. The bill passed 32-0 with a substitute. It goes to the House for concurrence or conference committee.
HB 239, sponsored by Rep. Terri Collins, R-Decatur, increases the salaries of public education employees by 2% and authorizes one-time bonuses for education retirees. The bill passed 33-0 with an amendment. It goes to the House for concurrence or conference committee.

HB 240, sponsored by Rep. Pebblin Warren, D-Tuskegee, makes an appropriation of $16 million from the Education Trust Fund to Tuskegee University for the support and maintenance of the educational program of the institution for fiscal year 2027. The bill passed 33-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 241, sponsored by Rep. Barbara Boyd, D-Anniston, makes an appropriation of $1.3 million from the Education Trust Fund to Talladega College for the support and maintenance of the educational program of the institution for fiscal year 2027. The bill passed 33-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 242, sponsored by Rep. Ed Oliver, R-Dadeville, makes an appropriation of $460,000 from the Education Trust Fund to Southern Preparatory Academy for the support and maintenance of the educational program of the institution for fiscal year 2027. The bill passed 33-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
HB 565, sponsored by Rep. Danny Garrett, R-Trussville, creates the College and Higher Education Excellence and Results (CHEER) Act to establish a program to provide bonus funding to higher education institutions that meet identified student and institution performance goals and objectives. The bill passed 33-0. It goes to Gov. Kay Ivey.
SB 380, sponsored by Sen. Arthur Orr, R-Decatur, gives retirees of the Teachers’ Retirement System a $1 per month served bonus, subject to any leftover revenue to the Education Trust Fund. The bill passed 33-0. It goes to the House.
SB 378, sponsored by Sen. Clyde Chambliss, R-Prattville, requires the Alabama Emergency Management Agency to administer the Alabama Dam Safety Program, replacing all responsibilities of local agencies. The bill passed 33-0. It goes to the House.
HB 487, sponsored by Rep. Rex Reynolds, R-Huntsville, makes supplemental appropriations in the amount of $43.1 million from the Opioid Treatment and Abatement Fund. The bill passed 34-0 with a substitute. It goes to the House for concurrence or conference committee.
